home.name: Francis Desjardins
home.enough: A dependency is easy to add and hard to remove, and most of what one does goes unused. The three libraries here ship none. The pages that demonstrate them take a router, a component kit and two renderers — a demo is not what gets shipped.

skills.title: What I build
skills.description: Framework-free cores with thin bindings over them. The core is plain TypeScript that runs in a browser, a worker or a service, and the binding is the only part that knows which — a test walks the import graph and fails if the core ever reaches a framework.
skills.thinking: None of this is a rule against libraries. It is one question, asked earlier than usual: how much of this one am I using? A draft library left here when it turned out all six stores it served mutated a flat object, where a spread does the same work. Software that runs for fifteen years pays for asking. A showcase never notices.
skills.secondary: Also: a self-declared cat person. No further questions.

work.title: What's running
work.description: Three pieces, each with a surface you can try. The names come from the shadows an eclipse casts. What they refuse to do is documented as carefully as the rest.

dialog.name: antumbra
dialog.description: Dialog manager on the native top layer. Zero shipped UI: the renderer stays yours. React, Solid and vanilla bindings.

boot.name: umbra
boot.description: Bootstrap orchestration, and not a front-end kind: the core needs no DOM, so one declared graph boots a page, a worker or a service. You say what each step needs; the parallelism is derived from that — no flag, no concurrency ceiling.

designSystem.name: penumbra
designSystem.description: The design system all three playgrounds wear — and the page that takes it apart, one layer at a time.
